strategy_title: Increasing XBLOCK via autotune caused 2.2x instruction bloat
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with larger XBLOCK configs (512–2048) to a memory-bound pointwise kernel caused a 29% latency regression despite improving achieved occupancy from 32.9% to 72.8%. The executed instruction count more than doubled (69M → 152M), indicating the autotune selected a configuration that introduced significant overhead—likely from the added xmask guard on every load/store (previously xmask=True was elided). The kernel became compute-bound (SM throughput 39% → 76%) rather than memory-latency-bound, but the extra compute work outweighed the latency-hiding benefit, and DRAM throughput actually dropped (26% → 20%), suggesting the larger tiles did not improve memory access efficiency.
slow_pseudocode:
# XBLOCK=128, grid=cdiv(N,128), xmask=True (elided)
xmask = tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1)
tmp11 = tl.load(ptr + idx, cond_mask, other=0.0)
tl.store(out + idx, result, None)
fast_pseudocode:
# autotune XBLOCK in {512,1024,2048}, xmask=xindex<xnumel
xmask = xindex < xnumel
tmp11 = tl.load(ptr + idx, mask=cond_mask & xmask, other=0.0)
tl.store(out + idx, result, mask=xmask)
applicable_when: Never: this specific combination of autotune + xmask introduction caused regression. Avoid applying this pattern to kernels where xnumel is exactly divisible by the original XBLOCK (making xmask=True valid and elided), as adding an explicit xmask reintroduces predication overhead across all memory ops.
do_not_apply_when: When the original kernel uses xmask=True (full tile, no boundary check needed) and xnumel is divisible by XBLOCK—adding an explicit xmask guard while also increasing XBLOCK doubles instruction count and causes compute-bound regression even if occupancy improves. Also avoid when the kernel is already latency-bound on L1TEX but the total work is small enough that instruction overhead dominates.
framework_notes: In Triton, when xnumel is exactly divisible by XBLOCK, the compiler elides the xmask predicate entirely (xmask=tl.full([XBLOCK], True, tl.int1) compiles to unconditional ops). Switching to xmask=xindex<xnumel forces predicated loads/stores on every instruction, roughly doubling instruction count for this kernel. The autotune also selected XBLOCK=256 (not the intended 512–2048), suggesting the autotuner found larger tiles worse and settled on a middle ground that still paid the xmask overhead without the full latency-hiding benefit.
